items.title: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting
items.description: Developments in the Gulf region amid the US-Israeli war on Iran came under discussion as the R4 foreign ministers — Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — met with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. The R4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran. According to the Foreign Office (FO), Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar participated in the first meeting between the R4 and France, Germany, Italy and the UK. “The meeting provided an opportunity for exchange of views on regional developments in the Gulf region, their social and economic impacts, and the urgent need to foster diplomatic engagement to resolve regional challenges of peace, security and stability,” it said. “Dar briefed his counterparts on the diplomatic and mediatory role Pakistan continues to play in de-escalating tensions, preventing resumption of hostilities and promoting peace. All ministers agreed for continued engagement in this format,” it said. The R4 bloc also held a separate meeting. According to the FO, Dar participated in the sixth R4 foreign ministers’ meeting alongside Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, and Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud of Saudi Arabia. The ministers reviewed developments in the region since their last meeting in New York in September, with “particular focus on the situation in the Middle East and related security challenges and conflicts”, the FO said. They expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their support for its sovereignty and territorial integrity. The FO added that the ministers also condemned the Houthi attacks targeting Saudi Arabia and underscored the importance of respecting state sovereignty. “They discussed ways to strengthen regional coordination and advance diplomatic efforts to promote lasting peace, security, and stability,” it said. Bilateral meetings Dar earlier held bilateral meetings with the Turkish and Egyptian foreign ministers, on the sidelines of the R4 meeting and a meeting between the R4 and European diplomats in Istanbul, the FO said. In a post on X, the FO said that Dar met with Fidan ahead of the ministerial meeting, thanking him for hosting the meetings. The pair discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, particularly the situation in the Middle East and Palestine. “They expressed concern over threats to regional stability and underscored the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and coordinated efforts to promote regional peace and security,” the FO statement said. Additionally, Dar and Fidan strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination on regional issues, including under the Makkah Defence Agreement. “Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood between Pakistan and Turkiye, and to deepening cooperation across all areas of mutual interest, both bilaterally and in multilateral fora,” the FO added. Later, the FO said that Dar also met with Egyptian FM Abdelatty on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting, where the two exchanged views on regional and international developments. In particular, they discussed the situation in Palestine and the Middle East, and underscored the importance of “sustained dialogue and diplomacy” in addressing challenges in the region. The two reaffirmed the “longstanding and fraternal ties” between Pakistan and Egypt, and highlighted the importance of sustained high-level engagement to further advance bilateral relations, the FO statement said. “They agreed to impart greater momentum to cooperation across a range of areas, including trade, business-to-business linkages, agriculture, pharmaceutical, connectivity, renewable energy, defence, and people-to-people exchanges,” the FO added. The ministers also reaffirmed their commitment to continued consultations and closer coordination under the R4 framework, as well as on matters of mutual interest, it said. The deputy premier later had a “warm and cordial meeting” with Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan, where he expressed Pakistan’s full support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom. “The two leaders reaffirmed the enduring strength of the fraternal ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and their commitment to further strengthening their strategic partnership through close cooperation across all areas of interest and regular consultations at all levels,” the FO said. They also underscored the “special bond” between their countries, reinforced by their bilateral Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia; as well as their shared commitment to regional peace, security and stability, it added. Separately, DPM Dar met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the meeting and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral ties “through sustained engagement and cooperation across multiple areas of mutual interest”, the FO said. According to the FO, the two ministers discussed relations between Pakistan and Germany and exchanged views on regional and international developments. They stressed the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and sustained international engagement to promote peace and stability and to address the evolving challenges in the region. Dar “welcomed the constructive engagement” of Germany, France, Italy and the UK with the R4 framework, the FO said, adding that he underscored the value of “continued consultations and diplomatic coordination on issues of shared concern”. Talks to revolve around Hormuz, Saudi Arabia British foreign minister Ed Miliband’s office said the talks would essentially revolve around “the Strait of Hormuz and the situation in Saudi Arabia”. It said Miliband “will advocate for a diplomatic solution to the (Hormuz) crisis that restores full navigational rights and freedoms”. He will also stress “how Iranian tactics are being replicated across the region, with attacks on Saudi Arabia further destabilising the region and increasing pressure on vital waterways and global chokepoints, such as Bab El-Mandeb and the Suez Canal”, it added. France confirmed the talks on “the Iranian crisis in its various ramifications”, hailing it as a first “in this format… against a backdrop of extreme instability and uncertainty in the region.” The meeting will aim to “strengthen coordination between Europeans and Middle Eastern countries in the face of crises that we did not choose and that affect us all,” the French foreign ministry said. A Turkish diplomatic source also told Reuters a day earlier that the seven countries would meet in the R4+E3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran , Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security. Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, the sources said. The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

items.title: When the guardians become the predators: Ghana’s child sexual abuse crisis
items.description: Seven children a day Every day this year, about seven Ghanaian girls aged between 10 and 14 have walked into a health facility pregnant. Read that again. Not young women. Girls. Children who should be learning fractions and fighting over skipping ropes, not preparing for labour wards. Between January and July 2026, the Ghana Health Service recorded 53,415 adolescent pregnancies across the country. Of these, 1,501 involved girls aged 10 to 14 . Under Ghanaian law, a child under 16 cannot consent to sex. So, every one of those 1,501 pregnancies is not a “teenage pregnancy”. It is evidence of defilement. It is child sexual abuse, with a medical record attached. And those are only the children whose abuse left a mark we can count. For every girl whose abuse ended in pregnancy, how many more carry it silently ; no pregnancy, no report, no file, no justice? This is the backdrop against which Ghana has spent the past fortnight reeling from allegations that a headmaster abused 19 of his own students. Before we talk about one school, we must understand the country it sits in. A global crisis with a Ghanaian face Ghana is not alone. According to UNICEF , 650 million girls and women alive today, 1 in 5 were subjected to sexual violence as children . Among boys and men, the figure is between 410 and 530 million, or about 1 in 7 . Look around any classroom, any church, any trotro. The survivors are among us. UNICEF defines sexual violence against a child as any deliberate, unwanted and non-essential act of a sexual nature, completed or attempted, that results in, or is highly likely to result in injury, pain or psychological suffering. By that standard, there is no such thing as a child “agreeing” to sex with an adult who holds power over her. There is no “relationship”. There is only violence. The Ghanaian picture is stark: Ghana, January – July 2026 Figure Adolescent pregnancies recorded at health facilities 53,415 Pregnancies among girls aged 10 to 14 1,501 Adolescent pregnancies in Upper East (first five months alone) 2,400+ Adolescent birth rate, Savannah Region 117.5 per 1,000 girls Sub-Saharan Africa average, for comparison 104 per 1,000 girls Projected national burden for the year 100,000+ Source: Ghana Health Service, presented at the National Multisectoral Dialogue on the Reduction of Teenage Pregnancy, Accra, 14 September 2026. The Ghana Health Service has noted something else worth underlining: adolescent pregnancies are far higher among girls who are out of school. School, in other words, is supposed to be a shield. It keeps girls learning, occupied, watched over and protected. Which makes the next question unbearable. What happens when the danger is inside the school gate? Even in school, children are not safe A recent review of publicly reported cases found at least 44 cases of teachers and heads of school accused of sexually abusing students in Ghana between January 2015 and October 2026 , involving at least 53 educators. Every accused teacher who could be identified was a man. What happened to those cases should trouble every parent: More than half; 23 of 44 , have no reported verdict or final sanction. They simply disappeared. Only 12 ended in a criminal conviction , almost all involving young pupils in basic schools. No head of a senior high school has ever been convicted. No dismissal of a teacher for sexual misconduct has been reported since 2019. Recent cases have stalled at interdiction, with no published outcome. Heads of school now feature in 4 of every 10 new cases , up from about 1 in 10 before 2025. Once a student turns 16, convictions all but vanish : only one of seven such cases ended in prison. Five of the six senior high school cases in 2025 and 2026 came to light through a phone video, a student speaking out or a journalist , not through the education system itself. Put plainly: the people at the very top of our schools are increasingly the ones accused, the system rarely finds them out on its own, and when it does, the cases tend to fade away. These are only the cases that became public. Victims and families who are afraid, ashamed or pressured never appear in any count. The real figure is certainly higher. This is the soil in which Obuasi grew. The bungalow at the top of the hill There is a house at the heart of every boarding school in Ghana. Parents point to it on admission day. It is where the headmaster lives, and it is meant to be the safest building on campus , the place a frightened child runs to when something goes wrong. At Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, that house now sits at the centre of a national scandal. An investigative documentary released this month alleges that the school’s headmaster, Dr Zakaria Abdulai, sexually harassed, assaulted and raped female students under his care. The number of girls tells its own story. At first, there were five. Then 14. Then 16. By mid-October, 19 students had reportedly come forward . Nineteen girls. Nineteen families. Nineteen futures. Let me be careful, as fairness and the law require. These are allegations. They have not been tested in court, and Dr Abdulai has declined to comment, citing ongoing investigations. On 13 October, the Minister for Education directed his suspension and asked the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ghana Police Service to investigate. The Ghana Education Service interdicted him the next day. He is entitled to due process. So are the girls. But there is a second story here that does not depend on any court verdict. It is the story of how long these girls were speaking , and how long the adults around them did nothing. How did Ghana get here? The very people entrusted with our children The most damning part of the Obuasi story is not a single act. It is the paper trail. Based on accounts that have emerged publicly, the warnings came early and often: Early 2025: The Obuasi West Municipal Chief Executive says she was told the headmaster had allegedly slept with a student. She invited the parents. The matter went no further. February 2026: The school’s own Girl Child Coordinator and a safeguarding teacher petitioned management over a growing number of complaints, asking for an urgent, impartial and confidential investigation. The petition was reportedly not acted on. March 2026: Five girls reported alleged sexual assault to the Municipal Education Directorate. Three put their complaints in writing. The Municipal Director has confirmed receiving them, explaining he fell seriously ill soon after. July 2026: The old students’ association petitioned for an investigation. Some parents reportedly withdrew complaints under pressure from opinion leaders who intervened on the headmaster’s behalf, claims some of those named dispute. 25 July 2026: Another alleged sexual abuse months after the authorities had been told. 5 August 2026: Students rioted, attacked the headmaster and damaged his bungalow. Six students were arrested. The school was shut. 13–14 October 2026: Only after the documentary reached the Minister was the headmaster suspended and interdicted. Read that list again. A safeguarding officer raised the alarm. Girls walked into a government office and wrote their complaints down. Old students petitioned. And still, it took a camera to move the system. The Ministry of Education has said it knew nothing until the documentary was brought to its attention. If that is true, it is not a defense. It is the indictment. It means complaints of sexual abuse against a head of school can sit in a district office for months without ever reaching the people with the power to act. This was also not the school’s first scandal. In 2018, a senior housemaster at the same school was dismissed over a similar case. And the headmaster also holds a constituency executive position in a political party, which has since asked him to withdraw from an internal election. When the accused holds power in both the school and the community, a girl’s complaint has to climb a very steep hill. How did we get here? We got here because we built schools where the person with the most power is also the person who decides whether complaints go anywhere. We got here because “settling” things quietly still feels, to too many families and opinion leaders, like the respectable thing to do. And we got here because our safeguarding systems exist on paper but break the moment the accused is important. Are we normalising rape? Does Ghana have a sexual abuse problem? Let me answer plainly: yes, Ghana has a sexual abuse problem. And in many quiet ways, we have normalised it. We normalise it when a sexual abuse case is “settled” at the family house because the accused is a relative, a pastor, a big man, or the family’s breadwinner. Police officers have pleaded with parents for years to stop settling defilement cases outside the station. We still do it. We normalise it with our language. A 15-year-old in a teacher’s bed is “in a relationship”. A headmaster accused of preying on students is “involved in a scandal”. A girl who speaks out is “bringing the school’s name into disrepute”. Words matter. When we soften the crime, we harden the silence. We normalise it when we ask the wrong questions. Why did she go to his house? What was she wearing? Why did she wait so long? A teacher controls a student’s grades, her references, her place in the dormitory, her chance at WASSCE. When he summons her, she goes. That is not consent. That is power. We normalise it when the law stops seeing children at 16. Once a student reaches the age of consent, convictions all but disappear. Yet a 17-year-old final-year student and her headmaster are not equals. Parliament should criminalise sexual relations between teachers and the students under their authority, whatever the student’s age. And we normalise it when a child protection story becomes a political football. Within days, Obuasi turned into a partisan fight over who shielded whom. Accountability for those who ignored complaints matters, whatever their party. But nineteen girls are not a campaign slogan. If the only lesson we learn is which side scored a point, we will be back here with another school and another bungalow. The Ghana Education Service has said that once culpability is established, the sanction is dismissal. Good. But a sanction that arrives only after a documentary goes viral is not a system. It is luck. When the cameras leave, who stays with these girls? Here is the question too few people are asking: what happens to these girls next month? Next year? In ten years? The news cycle will move on. It always does. The politicians will find a new fight. The documentary will become a link people forward once and forget. But the girls of Obuasi SHTS will still wake up in the same towns, walk past the same people who knew and said nothing, and carry memories no child should carry. Sexual abuse in childhood does not end when the abuse ends. Survivors face higher risks of depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress, substance misuse, school dropout and difficulty trusting anyone again. For girls in a small community, add stigma ; the whispering, the blame, the cruel jokes on WhatsApp. Too often in Ghana, it is the victim who changes schools, who stops going to church, who leaves town. There is also a practical crisis. The school was shut after the August riot, and students have reportedly been at home for nearly three months. The father of one alleged victim, a final-year student preparing for WASSCE, fears she may have to abandon her education unless she is placed in another school. He also alleges that some parents have been pressured to drop the case. So a girl who may have been abused is now also losing her education. That is a second violation, and this time the state is responsible. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection say it is working to locate and support the girls. That is welcome. But support must mean something specific: Trauma-informed counselling from trained psychologists or social workers ; free, confidential and sustained for as long as each girl needs it, not a single visit for the cameras. Medical care , including sexual and reproductive health services, at no cost to families. Guaranteed continuity of education : immediate placement in a school of each girl’s choice, with fees, boarding and WASSCE registration covered. Protection from intimidation , for the girls, their parents and the teachers who raised the alarm. Privacy . No names. No faces. No “exclusive interviews” with children. Every journalist, blogger and social media user has a duty here. Legal support , so that families who choose to pursue justice are not out-lawyered or out-waited. No one deserves to carry the shame of what was done to them. The shame belongs to the abuser and to every adult who looked away. Our job as a nation is to make sure these girls never have to carry it alone. Children must feel safe to learn. Here is what must change A child cannot learn in a building where she is afraid. Every parent who pays fees, buys a chop box and waves goodbye at a school gate is making an act of faith in the Ghanaian state. Obuasi has broken that faith. Restoring it will take more than one interdiction. 1. Take reporting out of the headmaster’s hands. Every school needs a confidential reporting channel that goes directly to an independent body outside the school’s chain of command. Complaints against heads of school must trigger automatic escalation to regional and national level within days. 2. Put deadlines on investigations. A complaint of sexual abuse should be investigated within weeks, not seasons. Any officer who sits on such a complaint should face sanctions. The Obuasi timeline shows exactly what delay costs: another alleged rape in July. 3. Audit our schools. Education policy advocates, including Eduwatch, have called for an independent, nationwide audit of teacher-student sexual misconduct. The government should commission it now and publish the results. 4. Publish outcomes. The Ghana Education Service should publish, every year, how many sexual misconduct complaints it received, how many it investigated, and how each ended. Silence after interdiction protects no one but the accused. 5. Close the age-16 loophole. Parliament should criminalise sexual relations between teachers and students under their authority, regardless of the student’s age. 6. End “settling”. Opinion leaders, chiefs, clergy and politicians who pressure families to drop sexual abuse complaints should be investigated for obstructing justice. 7. Fund survivor care. Psychosocial support for child survivors should be a funded line in the national budget, delivered through the Department of Social Welfare, the Ghana Health Service and trained school counsellors — not left to the goodwill of NGOs. 8. Teach children their rights. Age-appropriate education on bodily autonomy, consent and how to report abuse should reach every child in every school. To the girls of Obuasi SHTS, and to every child who has been hurt by someone who was meant to protect them: you deserved better. You still do. To the rest of us: the headmaster’s bungalow is not only in Obuasi. It is wherever a powerful adult is sure no one will listen to a child. Our task is to prove him wrong — not when the cameras are rolling, but every single day after they stop.

items.title: PLF 2027 : un budget défense de plus de 190 MMDH
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 prévoit un montant de 190,5 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au titre des dépenses que le ministre délégué chargé de l’Administration de la Défense nationale est autorisé à engager par anticipation sur les crédits qui seront ouverts au titre de l’année 2028. Cette enveloppe concerne le compte intitulé « Acquisition et réparation des matériels des Forces armées royales et soutien au développement de l’industrie de défense ». Le montant prévu pour 2027 dépasse celui inscrit dans le projet de loi de finances 2026, qui s’élevait à 157,171 MMDH. Il était de 133,453 MMDH en 2025 et de 124,766 MMDH en 2024. Cette évolution s’inscrit dans le cadre des efforts visant à moderniser les équipements des Forces armées royales et à développer l’industrie de défense nationale. À ce sujet, le ministre délégué chargé de l’Administration de la Défense nationale, Abdellatif Loudiyi, avait évoqué, lors du Salon international de l’aéronautique de Marrakech 2026, les efforts engagés pour renforcer le cadre juridique, attirer les investissements et favoriser le transfert de technologies et le développement des capacités industrielles nationales. Le développement de cette industrie constitue également un enjeu de souveraineté nationale. Dans son discours du Trône, le Roi Mohammed VI avait souligné l’importance de la mise en place d’une base industrielle de défense et de cybersécurité, susceptible de contribuer au renforcement de la souveraineté du Royaume, à la création d’emplois et au développement économique. The post PLF 2027 : un budget défense de plus de 190 MMDH appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Fintiri relaxes curfew in Lamurde, restricts movement from 9pm to 6am
items.description: Gov. Ahmadu Fintiri of Adamawa has further relaxed the curfew imposed on Lamurde Local Government Area from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. ‎ ‎The development was contained in a statement on Friday in Yola by Mr Humwashi Wonosikou, Chief Press Secretary to the Governor.‎ ‎ According to the statement, the review followed reports of sustained calm and improved security in the area after the recent crisis. ‎ ‎Fintiri said movement is now unrestricted during the day, while the curfew will be observed daily from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. ‎ ‎”The curfew relaxation followed cooperation of affected residents and efforts by Security Agencies. ‎ ‎”However, Government would not condone any attempt to disrupt the peace achieved so far,” Fintiri warned. ‎ ‎He said security operatives had been directed to remain vigilant and ensure strict compliance with the curfew. ‎ ‎The governor who reiterated his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property, called on traditional rulers and relevant stakeholders in the community to sustain peace and embrace dialogue in resolving differences. ‎ ‎”Adamawa remains known for tolerance and unity; I therefore urged stakeholders to preserve the reputation,” Fintiri maintained. ‎ ‎The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that two communities in the area were involved in repeated clashes over land dispute.(NAN) ‎ The post Fintiri relaxes curfew in Lamurde, restricts movement from 9pm to 6am appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Un « programme Captain America pour chiens » : au Texas, une start-up veut modifier génétiquement les auxiliaires canins de l’armée américaine
items.description: Warhound, une nouvelle start-up américaine créée par le cofondateur d’Anduril, Palmer Luckey, et Ben Lamm, à la tête de Colossal Biosciences, une entreprise de biotechnologie qui veut faire renaître des espèces disparues, comme le mammouth laineux, a obtenu 200 millions de dollars de financement pour cloner et modifier génétiquement des « chiens de guerre » destinés à l’armée et aux forces de l’ordre américaines Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear », TechCrunch , 22 octobre 2026.'> 1 . L’entreprise sera dirigée par David Spirk, un vétéran du corps des Marines, ancien premier directeur des données du Pentagone et conseiller chez Palantir, l’entreprise de surveillance cofondée par Peter Thiel. Warhound revendique être « certifiée par l’American Humane Society », une organisation américaine dédiée au bien-être animal, et qu’elle permettra à terme de limiter le nombre de chiens soumis à un entraînement intensif inutile What is Warhound, Palmer Luckey's war dog startup that just emerged from stealth ? », Business Insider , 23 octobre 2026.'> 2 . En février, l’inspection générale du Pentagone avait pointé du doigt dans un rapport les mauvaises conditions d’hébergement des chiens militaires dans les chenils de douze bases du pays, liées à la mort de quatre d’entre eux entre 2021 et 2023. Vidéo mise en ligne sur le site de Warhound. La création de Warhound repose sur un constat : plus de 80 % des chiens de l’armée américaine sont importés d’Europe, selon l'entreprise, et moins de la moitié sont jugés aptes au service. Or, ces animaux sont encore utilisés à large échelle pour des missions de détection d’explosifs, de recherche ou d’autres tâches jugées trop dangereuses pour les humains ou trop difficiles pour les machines. Warhound prévoit ainsi de sélectionner les chiens considérés comme les plus performants, de conserver leurs cellules dans une biobanque puis de les cloner. Leurs gènes seront ensuite modifiés afin d’accroître leur longévité et d’améliorer leur santé et leurs performances. Sur son site, la start-up, installée au Texas, vante « une nouvelle race de domination […] construite pour la victoire ». Luckey évoquait déjà en 2023 la possibilité de modifier génétiquement des chiens pour les besoins de l’armée. Dans un épisode de podcast auquel participait notamment Jacob Helberg, nommé sous-secrétaire d’État aux affaires économiques par Trump en janvier 2025, Luckey déclarait : « Vous pensez que des bergers allemands de 70 kilos font de bonnes unités canines ? Et des loups sinistres ( « direwolves » ) de 270 kilos qui portent 70 kilos d’armure ? […] Ils sont éteints pour le moment, mais ils ne doivent pas nécessairement le rester ». Anduril Founder @PalmerLuckey spoke about this in 2023 : “You could give every canine unit the characteristics of the strongest Arctic Wolf that ever walked the earth.” “How about Dire Wolves ? 600-pound canines units carrying 150 pounds of armor.” pic.twitter.com/KGqyzBtJQO https://t.co/BsbQPq6pWb — Jawwwn (@jawwwn_) October 22, 2026 En plus de modifier le patrimoine génétique des chiens afin de les rendre plus performants et plus résistants, Warhound affirme vouloir les équiper de technologies de pointe, produites par Anduril, afin de leur fournir une « conscience situationnelle sur le champ de bataille ». Ben Lamm le résume ainsi : il s’agit d’un « programme Captain America pour les chiens » Palmer Luckey unveils start-up to breed ‘genetically enhanced’ dogs for military », Financial Times , 23 octobre 2026.'> 3 . L’article Un « programme Captain America pour chiens » : au Texas, une start-up veut modifier génétiquement les auxiliaires canins de l’armée américaine est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: SIAO 2026 : Plus de 6 000 exposants et une trentaine de pays attendus
items.description: À l’approche de la 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, le comité d’organisation a animé une conférence de presse, le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, sur le site du SIAO à Ouagadougou. Objectif : dresser l’état d’avancement des préparatifs. « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ? », tel est le thème retenu pour cette 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Le Presidium… À une semaine de l’ouverture, le comité d’organisation a dévoilé les principales innovations de cette édition. Parmi celles-ci figurent la tenue d’ateliers thématiques destinés à mieux vulgariser les métiers de l’artisanat au Village artisanal de Ouagadougou (VAO), la création d’un nouvel espace baptisé « Village du pays invité d’honneur », l’augmentation du nombre de portes d’entrée et de sortie du site, ainsi que l’organisation d’activités sportives. Le Ghana est le pays invité d’honneur de cette 18e édition, placée sous le très haut patronage du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Plus de 6 000 exposants et une trentaine de pays attendus. Minute.bf

items.title: CBG calls for increased climate finance to scale nature-based solutions in Ghana
items.description: Consolidated Bank Ghana (CBG) has identified limited access to finance, grants and donor support as major barriers to scaling up nature-based solutions in Ghana and across Africa. The bank’s Head of Sustainable Financing and Impact Department, Mrs Eva Ackuaku, says although such projects can deliver environmental and social benefits, concerns about their commercial viability often make it difficult for them to secure conventional bank financing. Speaking at the Africa Climate Dialogue 2026, she called for increased financial support, an enabling policy environment and stronger collaboration among financial institutions and development partners to unlock investment in nature-based solutions. Mrs Ackuaku said financing must become central to climate discussions if proposed solutions are to move beyond conversations to practical implementation. She explained that banks must conduct due diligence before financing projects because the funds they manage belong to depositors and other customers. This responsibility, she said, requires financial institutions to assess the viability of projects even when they promise significant environmental and social benefits. “The major setback that I see is limited access to finance,” she said. According to her, grants, donor funding and financial guarantees could help bridge the funding gap by supporting projects that struggle to demonstrate sufficient commercial viability to attract conventional bank financing. Beyond financing, Mrs Ackuaku identified land ownership as another challenge facing some carbon projects, particularly those located outside major cities. She said disputes or uncertainties over land ownership could complicate project development and make it more difficult for initiatives to attract investment. She urged governments to establish policies that support climate investments while aligning with national and international priorities. “Governments need to create that conducive environment for us. The policies must align with national priorities, international priorities,” she said. Mrs Ackuaku added that projects seeking financing must demonstrate sound governance structures, appropriate policies and procedures, and effective risk management. She explained that banks assess financial models under different scenarios to determine how projects might perform when conditions deteriorate. These assessments help lenders establish whether a project can withstand potential risks and generate sufficient returns to justify financing. CBG calls for stronger partnerships Mrs Ackuaku also called for greater collaboration among financial institutions, research institutions, development finance institutions and donor partners to mobilise resources for nature-based solutions. She said banks should work together to expand access to funding rather than compete for the same resources. “We do not compete, but we collaborate,” she said. She added that partnerships extending beyond the banking sector could help stakeholders identify funding opportunities and advance climate-related initiatives that might otherwise struggle to secure investment. Nature-based solutions use the protection, restoration or sustainable management of ecosystems to address environmental challenges while delivering benefits to people and communities. Such initiatives can include forest restoration, wetland conservation and mangrove protection. However, their ability to attract investment can depend on clear land rights, credible project governance, measurable outcomes and financing arrangements that address the risks faced by lenders and investors. Mrs Ackuaku also disclosed that CBG was preparing to showcase its sustainability activities through an upcoming Sustainability Week celebration, aimed at increasing public awareness of the bank’s work in the sector. The Africa Climate Dialogue 2026 brought together stakeholders to discuss how climate finance, carbon markets and private-sector investment could help scale up nature-based solutions in Ghana and across Africa.

items.title: Samartex Timber and Plywood Company reels under galamsey as illegal miners cut into its operations and livelihoods
items.description: Samartex Timber and Plywood Company Limited is raising concerns about the increasing threat of illegal mining to its core operations. Management says the company’s concessions have come under attack, as the expansion of unregulated mining disrupts its timber harvest and water production. Managers tell Joynews the operations of illegal miners have forced the company to suspend a multi-million cedi ecotourism project. Several residents of Wassa Amenfi West Municipality depend largely on Samartex for employment, as the company maintains over 2,000 employees. But illegal mining activities are severely compromising the company’s long-term harvesting plans. The miners are eating into the concessions of Samartex as hundreds of commercially valued tree species are decimated before harvest teams could arrive. “Mining is really impacting our activities and our livelihoods. One, now places that we have earmarked for harvesting are now non-existent, it’s no more there, because we make plans before we go anywhere we harvest our trees. And this is the case, you make plans that this year I’ll go here and before you get there the resource is gone,” Head of Forestry, Justice Eshun told Joynews. The illegal mining activities have affected the forest resources but the company’s water infrastructure, as water treatment from the Tano River for both internal industrial use and for surrounding communities has come to a halt. “Our water source, were depending on the Tano and treating it for use in the company and also in the in the communities. But now the Tano is such that when you want to treat it for human use, then the cost is just too outrageous, so we cannot depend on that Tano River anymore,” Mr. Eshun said. Apart from the pollution of the Tano River driving the cost of water treatment, a situation which has forced the company to invest heavily in sinking of boreholes, the environmental degradation has also derailed ambitious ecotourism initiatives centered on the Tano River. Head of the Forestry Department at Samartex, Justice Eshun, says Samartex had earlier engaged the services of an expert from Brazil to assess and develop a major eco-project featuring Canopy houses on trees along the Tano Riverbanks. “We are struggling to even get workers to work in the company because the mining is not regulated, people just go in for easy money and they think that is what they have to do. So now, even getting workers to work is also a big challenge that we are facing”. Overwhelmed by the invasion, the management of Samartex has been supporting the operations of the Forestry Commission’s Rapid Response Team to deal with the influx. Though 100 illegal miners are arrested each month, officials are unhappy over the slow pace of prosecution. Mr. Eshun explains: “We even brought an expert from Brazil to do the assessment, but we couldn’t continue because of the current state of the stream. When you come to Samatex now, we have a structure along the Tano built totally from wood; it’s such a beautiful thing, but now it can only be there as a white elephant because nobody will come and see a brown Tano River. So that is the challenge. All our dream; all the things that we wanted to do in terms of ecotourism has been dashed because of the current state of the resources or the Tano River.” The clear waters of the Tano River, which revealed white stones underneath it 15 years ago, have now turned brown due to heavy siltation and pollution.

items.title: GJA President Albert Dwumfour praises Ga Mantse over 2021 election dispute
items.description: The President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, has commended the Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, for helping resolve an electoral dispute that stalled the Association’s leadership transition in 2021. Mr Dwumfour said the traditional ruler’s intervention helped end a legal impasse that had halted the GJA’s electoral process for nearly a year. He made the remarks on Friday, October 23, during a courtesy visit by a GJA delegation to the Ga Mantse Palace in Accra. Mr Dwumfour recalled that the Association’s elections, originally scheduled for 2020, were postponed to 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 general elections. The process was subsequently halted by a court injunction, leaving the Association unable to proceed with the elections. “In 2021, the association was faced with a major challenge. “Our election was supposed to be taking place in 2020, but for COVID and for the election 2020, we moved it to 2021. We were hit with a court injunction, and it was stopped. Everything, in fact, the process was halted for almost a year,” he said. Mr Dwumfour said the Ga Mantse intervened by inviting the parties involved and facilitating efforts to resolve the disagreement. He credited the traditional ruler’s experience and mediation efforts with helping the Association overcome the impasse. “So His Royal Majesty, you stepped in, you called us, you invited us to your house. I remember I later invited all the parties together with Justice Julia, former Justice of the High Court. You were able to use your wisdom and a fountain of experience to mediate, resolve the statement, and we were able to move ahead,” he stated. Mr Dwumfour also expressed the GJA’s readiness to collaborate with the Ga Traditional Council on awards initiatives, including the Ga State’s Sacred Crown Awards. He said the Association was prepared to work with the Ga Mantse and the Council to organise the event. “I can tell you without mincing words that together with my national executives, we are ready to partner your leadership and the Ga Traditional Council to organise this special award,” he said. The GJA President further announced that President John Dramani Mahama had confirmed his participation as keynote speaker at the 30th GJA Awards. He said the Speaker of Parliament and the Chief Justice were also expected to attend, while Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II would serve as patron of the awards. The ceremony is scheduled for November 7, 2026, to recognise excellence in journalism and honour practitioners whose work has contributed to public-interest reporting and the development of Ghana’s media landscape.

items.title: Innovation, financement et résilience climatique: l’État engage des réflexions sur le logement
items.description: Dakar abrite depuis hier, jeudi 22 octobre, le Salon international de l’habitat, du logement et de la construction au Sénégal, qui porte sur le thème : « L’habitat souverain : Sunu dekkuwaay ». Cette rencontre de trois jours a pour but de créer des ponts entre acteurs du secteur de l’habitat afin de promouvoir un accès au logement décent et durable et un développement urbain mieux maîtrisé. Placé sous le thème : « L’habitat souverain : Sunu dekkuwaay », le Salon international de l’habitat, du logement et de la construction au Sénégal s’est ouvert hier, jeudi 22 octobre, à Dakar, pour trois jours d'échanges et de partenariat. L'objectif de cette édition est de promouvoir des solutions adaptées aux réalités locales fondées sur le transfert de compétences, la planification urbaine, l'innovation, le financement adapté et la résilience climatique. Selon Moussa Bala Fofana, ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire, l’habitat est une condition fondamentale de la dignité humaine, un droit social inaliénable. Pour lui, « à Dakar, plus d'un ménage sur deux est locataire et le poids écrasant des loyers étouffe les budgets des familles ». Poursuivant, il a rappelé que les inondations récurrentes, la précarité des quartiers sous-équipés et la tragédie dramatique des effondrements d’immeubles « sont les symptômes d’une urbanisation anarchique et non maîtrisée dans nos villes ». Cependant, le ministre estime qu’une ville doit naître d'une vision stratégique, d'un aménagement préalable et d'investissements cohérents. Les citoyens doivent accéder au logement abordable via l'achat direct, la location-vente ou la location encadrée. Dans cette perspective, Moussa Bala Fofana a fait savoir que dans chaque projet agréé, l’État exige un équilibre républicain de 50 % de logements sociaux et abordables et de 50 % de logements libres, garantissant à la fois la solidarité sociale et la rentabilité économique des investisseurs. Astou Rose Gaye, directrice générale de la Banque de l’habitat du Sénégal (Bhs), pense que l’accès à un logement décent ne doit pas être un privilège. À l’heure actuelle, dit-elle, le Sénégal doit produire des habitations qui répondent aux attentes légitimes des Sénégalais tout en restant compatibles avec leur pouvoir d'achat. Un conseil interministériel sur le logement prévu Selon Moussa Bala Fofana, il est prévu, en fin octobre, la tenue d’un conseil interministériel sur le logement, l’organisation de la table ronde des bailleurs et investisseurs au début du mois de novembre 2026 et la pose de la première pierre de la nouvelle Ville de Thiès en mi-décembre 2026. Le ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire a aussi annoncé qu’à Dakar, Pikine, Guédiawaye, Thiès et Saint-Louis, le plan de restructuration urbaine cible 300 hectares pour générer 45.000 logements décents, soutenus par un investissement prévisionnel de 1100 milliards de FCfa sur 15 ans. Face à la menace des édifices dégradés, l’État, informe-t-il, a lancé le Plan national de traitement des bâtiments menaçant ruine. D’après lui, un audit identifie 14.000 constructions à diagnostiquer à l'échelle nationale. Pour le ministre, « rien qu’à Dakar, notamment à la Médina, Colobane, Biscuiterie et Grand Dakar, une première tranche d’urgence de 14 opérations prioritaires pour 24,6 milliards de FCfa est engagée dans le but de reconstruire et reloger en toute sécurité ». Pour résorber le déficit national, estimé à 500.000 logements, la feuille de route, indique M. Fofana, vise la production annuelle régulière de 33.000 logements, injectant ainsi près de 800 milliards de FCfa par an dans l'économie nationale. Bada MBATHIE

items.title: Bonya community celebrates as Techiman North MP fulfills promise with new CHPS Compound
items.description: The people of Bonya can finally breathe a collective sigh of relief. After years of enduring difficult journeys to access basic healthcare, the community has officially received a fully furnished CHPS Compound, marking the end of a long struggle for medical services. For residents of this farming community, accessing healthcare has always been an arduous task. Women and children, in particular, bore the brunt of this challenge, often traveling long distances to Techiman for medical attention. The situation was most critical during childbirth. Many expectant mothers recounted the terrifying experience of traveling to Techiman while in labor. Some women were forced to deliver at home, and tragically, in some cases, babies were lost due to the lack of nearby medical facilities. The journey to today’s commissioning began when community members approached their Member of Parliament, Elizabeth Ofosu Adjare, with two key requests: a health facility and a school building. According to the MP, she explained to the community that while she could immediately deliver a school block, the CHPS compound would have to wait until the National Democratic Congress (NDC) was voted into power. True to her word, within two years of the NDC assuming office, that promise has been fulfilled. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister expressed her satisfaction at delivering on her commitment to the people of Bonya. “When I came here, they asked for a school and a health facility. I told them I could only do the school block at the time, but the CHPS compound had to wait until the NDC was in power. I made a promise, and today, that promise has been fulfilled,” she said. The MP emphasized that the project is aimed at improving access to quality healthcare for residents, ensuring that no woman has to risk her life or her child’s life simply to give birth. The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, who joined the MP for the commissioning, urged community members to take ownership of the facility. He called on residents to protect the infrastructure and ensure its proper maintenance for the benefit of both present and future generations. “This is your facility. Protect it. Maintain it. It is for your benefit and the benefit of your children,” he advised. The District Director of Health, Mr. Kumah Alexander, elaborated on the importance of the fully furnished facility to healthcare delivery in the area. He noted that the compound is equipped to handle basic maternal and child health cases, significantly reducing the burden on the district hospital and improving health outcomes for the community. In a further boost to healthcare delivery in the area, the MP presented a brand-new motorcycle to the facility. The donation is expected to ease the movement of health staff, particularly during emergencies when time is of the essence. For the mothers and children of Bonya, the new CHPS Compound represents more than just a building—it symbolizes safety, dignity, and a brighter future. The facility stands as a testament to what can be achieved when promises are kept, and communities are prioritized.

items.title: GAF to stage land combat firepower demonstration at Bundase on October 30
items.description: The Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) will hold its 2026 Land Combat Firepower Demonstration at the Battle Training Camp in Bundase on Friday, October 30. The annual field demonstration is organised for students of the Ghana Armed Forces Command and Staff College. A press release issued by the Department of Public Relations, signed by Captain Veronica Adzo Arhin, Acting Director-General, said government officials, defence attachés, military personnel and other invited guests would attend the exercise. The demonstration will involve live firing of heavy weapons, battle drills and other tactical manoeuvres. The GAF has, therefore, urged residents of Bundase and its environs not to panic upon hearing gunfire and explosions during rehearsals and the main exercise. It assured the public that all necessary safety measures had been put in place to protect people in the area and appealed for their cooperation.

items.title: Lutte contre la Diphtérie : Kédougou renforce la riposte contre l’épidémie
items.description: Un projet d’urgence de 60 jours a été lancé hier à Kédougou pour renforcer la vaccination, sensibiliser les populations et améliorer la détection précoce des cas de diphtérie. Soutenue par le fonds Start Network, cette initiative vient en appui aux actions déjà engagées par l’État. Présidant la rencontre de lancement, le préfet de Kédougou, El Hadji Malick Sémou Diouf, a souligné l’importance de la mobilisation des acteurs et des communautés pour freiner la propagation de la maladie, dont des cas ont été confirmés dans la région depuis août. Il a également invité les populations à se rapprocher rapidement des structures sanitaires en cas de signes suspects. Mis en œuvre par Kédougou Encadrement et Orientation du Développement Humain (KEOH), en collaboration avec les autorités sanitaires, le projet couvre cinq régions du Sénégal, dont Kédougou, Dakar, Louga, Thiès et Diourbel. Selon Djaliba Tandian, manager de KEOH, l’intervention vise à combler les insuffisances de moyens et à soutenir les activités prévues par les services sanitaires. Une centaine de relais communautaires seront ainsi identifiés, formés et accompagnés pour intensifier la sensibilisation. Le projet prévoit également un appui aux équipes mobiles de vaccination afin de vérifier le statut vaccinal des enfants et de compléter les doses manquantes, y compris pour ceux qui ne sont pas encore vaccinés. L’objectif est de renforcer la prévention et de contribuer à enrayer la propagation de la diphtérie. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: «Haute trahison» : Mariani réagit sur RT à l’alliance de Kabila avec le M23 en RDC
items.description: Le 12 octobre, a Goma, le Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) a devoile sa direction. Joseph Kabila, president de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC) entre 2001 et 2019, en prend la tete. Dans les rangs de ce nouveau mouvement figurent Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa et Sultani Makenga, trois responsables associes a l'AFC/M23. Ce dernier controle Goma et mene des combats contre l'armee congolaise. Presente comme une alternative au pouvoir de Kinshasa, le FRN associe ainsi l'ancien chef d'etat a des figures de la rebellion. C'est sur cette alliance que RT a interroge Thierry Mariani. Une comparaison avec Charles de Gaulle Mariani precise que le jugement sur l'ancien president revient d'abord aux Congolais. « Je dis simplement que, quand je vois l'attitude de M. Kabila, je pense que c'est aux Congolais de le juger », a-t-il explique. Il a ensuite rapproche la situation de l'histoire de France. « Est-ce que vous imaginez, pendant la Deuxieme Guerre mondiale, le general de Gaulle s'allier avec l'Allemagne nazie qui occupait une partie du territoire de la France pour prendre le pouvoir en France ? », a demande l'eurodepute. « ecoutez, si c'etait en France, on appellerait ca une haute trahison, et ca merite le châtiment qu'on connaît » , a-t-il declare. Pour Mariani, un dirigeant qui s'associe a un mouvement occupant une partie de son pays ne peut se presenter comme son liberateur. Les relations entre Paris et Kigali evoquees Mariani a egalement ete interroge sur la reaction des capitales europeennes a la situation dans l'est de la RDC. Il attribue leur retenue a la place qu'occupe encore le genocide de 1994 dans les relations avec le Rwanda. « Et comme cette rente memorielle, pour reprendre une expression de M. Macron, est la, les Occidentaux, les Europeens n'osent pas reagir », a-t-il affirme. L'eurodepute a ensuite parle des rencontres entre Emmanuel Macron et Paul Kagame. « Regardez ce qui se passe. M. Macron a recu de multiples fois M. Kagame a l'elysee, c'est meme l'un de ses presque plus proches amis en Afrique, et il ne fait rien », a-t-il declare. Mariani considere que les relations politiques avec Kigali influencent la reponse europeenne aux evenements dans l'est congolais. Son entretien a RT intervient alors que la creation du FRN a replace le role de Joseph Kabila et les rapports avec le Rwanda dans le debat politique en RDC.

items.title: Le sommet Corée du Nord–États-Unis de 2026 : que négocier et que préserver ?
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (PDF) L’un des principaux facteurs susceptibles de déterminer l’évolution de la péninsule coréenne au second semestre 2026 est la volonté de plus en plus ouvertement affichée par le président américain Donald Trump de renouer avec la diplomatie des sommets avec Kim Jong-un, président de la Commission des affaires d’État de la Corée du Nord. Le 16 août, en ordonnant une réduction substantielle des exercices militaires conjoints entre la Corée du Sud et les États-Unis, Donald Trump a directement évoqué sa « très bonne relation » avec Kim Jong-un ; trois jours plus tard, il a publiquement déclaré vouloir le rencontrer avant la fin de l’année. Ces déclarations dépassent le registre de la simple rhétorique : elles montrent que la Maison-Blanche a inscrit la possibilité d’un sommet à son agenda diplomatique concret. L’article Le sommet Corée du Nord–États-Unis de 2026 : que négocier et que préserver ? est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

Breaking: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapse
items.description: Concern is growing around Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany after Bild reported that the Belgian manager was taken to a hospital in Munich by ambulance on Friday. According to the report, a helicopter had landed earlier at Bayern’s training ground on Säbener Straße. Further details about the circumstances surrounding the incident have not yet been confirmed. Sky Germany is reporting that Kompany collapsed at training. Kompany had been battling a severe illness (reported to be a viral infection) and a hip issue ahead of Bayern Munich’s Champions League game against Arsenal, but he was cleared to return to the bench. Bayern Munich is now preparing for Sunday’s Bundesliga clash against SC Freiburg following Wednesday’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League. The most important thing is Kompany’s health and well-being. Understandably, Bayern Munich supporters are hoping that the situation is not serious and that the 40-year-old coach is receiving the care he needs. There is no confirmed information yet regarding the reason for his hospitalization or whether it will affect his availability for Sunday’s match.

items.title: 2027: NDC guber candidate pledges to industrialise Delta
items.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Governorship Candidate Mr Chris Iyovwaye, has pledged to drive industrialisation as vehicle for job creation and sustainable development in the state if elected in 2027. Iyovwaye made the pledge during a consultation with Chief Emmanuel Nwachukwu, Managing Director, Benco Pools, and his grassroots movement on Friday in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area of Delta. The NDC delegation, led by Iyovwaye, includes the party’s Delta North senatorial candidate, Mr Victor Ochei, and other candidates from Ika Federal Constituency. Others were the party’s candidates for Ika North-East Constituency I, Mr Sylvester Chukwuedo, and Ika South Constituency, Mrs Ogor Tony-Obuh. Iyovwaye criticised poor management of Delta’s common patrimony and the lack of innovative leadership capable of translating resources into tangible benefits. He said industrialisation would drive economic growth, create employment and promote sustainable development if supported by practical policies and measurable results. The governorship candidate said the NDC remained committed to changing the state’s development trajectory through policies that would unlock its economic potentials. Iyovwaye also expressed confidence in the quality of the party’s candidates across all levels, including its presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. He called for the support of Nwachukwu and his associates, saying Delta has greater economic potential than the reflected current level of development. Also, Ochei thanked Nwachukwu for receiving the delegation and recalled his earlier visit to the business leader a few days before the consultation. He described the developing relationship as a partnership with the potential to benefit all parties, particularly the people. The other candidates outlined their commitment to effective representation and development and reinforced the delegation’s message of coordinated engagement across Ika Federal Constituency and Delta North. The party’s Delta North Senatorial Chairman, Mr Aaron Ebenuwa, also led members of the party leadership on the visit. The post 2027: NDC guber candidate pledges to industrialise Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Énergie solaire : Orange Énergies mise sur le paiement échelonné pour élargir l’accès à l’électricité
items.description: Orange Énergies Burkina Faso a présenté ses solutions d’accès aux énergies renouvelables et ses outils de gestion énergétique, le 22 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. À travers des kits solaires payables en plusieurs mensualités et une plateforme numérique de gestion de l’énergie, l’entreprise entend faciliter l’accès à l’électricité pour les ménages et les petits entrepreneurs, notamment dans les zones confrontées à une insuffisance de l’approvisionnement électrique. Pour la responsable d’Orange Énergies, Nafila Dabiré/Sangaré, l’accès à l’énergie constitue un prolongement des services numériques proposés par le groupe. « Pour que tous ces services fonctionnent, il faut de l’énergie. Il faut un téléphone qui soit chargé, il faut un ordinateur qui soit chargé » , a-t-elle expliqué. Elle a souligné que les besoins concernent aussi bien les familles souhaitant éclairer leur logement que les entrepreneurs ayant besoin d’électricité pour poursuivre leurs activités. Orange Énergies propose des équipements comprenant notamment des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et des ampoules. Ces kits permettent de recharger des téléphones et des ordinateurs, de disposer d’un éclairage et, selon les modèles, d’alimenter certains équipements professionnels utilisés dans les salons de coiffure, les ateliers de couture ou les petites boutiques. L’entreprise mise sur le paiement échelonné pour rendre ces équipements plus accessibles aux ménages dont les moyens financiers ne permettent pas un achat au comptant. Selon Nafila Dabiré/Sangaré, un kit vendu à 200 000 francs CFA au comptant peut être acquis moyennant un premier versement de 35 000 francs CFA, suivi de mensualités de 10 000 francs CFA pendant la durée prévue par l’offre. Le montant total atteint alors 225 000 francs CFA dans le cadre de la formule de paiement à tempérament présentée. La responsable a précisé que les clients peuvent se procurer ces équipements auprès du réseau de distribution d’Orange Burkina Faso. Elle a également annoncé que les solutions Orange Énergies comptent plus de 180 000 bénéficiaires au Burkina Faso. Une plateforme pour gérer la distribution de l’énergie-©Faso7 Au-delà des kits destinés aux ménages, Orange Énergies a présenté Orange Smart Énergie, également appelée OSE. Cette plateforme permet notamment de gérer la distribution de l’électricité, de suivre la consommation et de faciliter les paiements pour les installations équipées de compteurs connectés. Le dispositif s’adresse également aux acteurs qui exploitent des mini-réseaux électriques dans les localités éloignées. Grâce à des compteurs intelligents associés à la plateforme, les utilisateurs peuvent acheter de l’électricité à distance et effectuer leurs paiements via un service de paiement mobile, sans avoir à se déplacer pour régler leur consommation. L’entreprise travaille avec des fournisseurs et des partenaires spécialisés pour sélectionner les équipements compatibles avec sa plateforme. Elle ne fabrique donc pas elle-même les kits présentés, mais s’appuie sur ces collaborations pour les rendre accessibles à travers son réseau commercial. Des partenariats locaux recherchés-©Faso7 Orange Énergies souhaite également élargir son réseau de partenaires au Burkina Faso. Nafila Dabiré/Sangaré a invité les entreprises locales proposant des solutions énergétiques adaptées à prendre contact avec la structure afin d’étudier leur éventuelle intégration à son offre. « Nos attentes effectivement au niveau local, c’est vraiment d’avoir un vivier de partenaires qui nous proposent des solutions qui soient compatibles avec notre plateforme » , a déclaré la responsable. Les besoins évoqués concernent notamment les équipements destinés aux activités génératrices de revenus, comme le pompage agricole, la conservation par le froid et certains appareils professionnels, ainsi que les solutions de cuisson propre. « L’objectif, c’est d’être hyper inclusif pour l’énergie verte, de permettre à tout Burkinabè d’avoir accès à l’énergie » , a déclaré Nafila Dabiré/Sangaré. À travers ces offres, Orange Énergies entend rapprocher les services numériques et l’accès à l’électricité. L’enjeu consiste à proposer des équipements adaptés aux capacités financières des utilisateurs, tout en assurant leur accompagnement pendant la période de remboursement. La diversification des solutions et le développement de partenariats locaux devraient contribuer à élargir les usages des énergies renouvelables au Burkina Faso. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Énergie solaire : Orange Énergies mise sur le paiement échelonné pour élargir l’accès à l’électricité est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Région de Dakar : Suspension temporaire des «Navétanes» à compter du 26 octobre
items.description: Le Gouverneur de la région de Dakar a suspendu, jusqu’à nouvel ordre, les rencontres de football populaire communément appelées « Navétanes », ainsi que les activités qui leur sont directement liées. La mesure est applicable à l’ensemble de la région, à partir du lundi 26 octobre 2026. Dans un arrêté signé le 23 octobre 2026, le Gouverneur de la région de Dakar, Ousmane Kane, a ordonné la suspension temporaire des rencontres de Navétanes sur toute l’étendue du territoire régional. Cette décision intervient dans un contexte marqué par les impératifs de sécurité liés à l’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026, qui mobilisent d’importantes ressources des forces de défense et de sécurité. Elle vise notamment à prévenir les risques d’affrontements entre supporters et de dégradations de biens publics et privés, tout en préservant l’ordre public et la sécurité des personnes et des biens durant cet événement international, souligne l'arrêté. Les préfets des départements de Dakar, Pikine, Guédiawaye, Rufisque et Keur Massar sont chargés de veiller à l’application de cette mesure, en coordination avec les autorités municipales, les forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que les responsables des structures d’organisation des Navétanes, souligne l’arrêté.

items.title: Orientation scolaire : une situation mitigée dans l’académie de Dakar
items.description: À Dakar, l'orientation de nouveaux élèves en classe de 6e constitue un défi pour plusieurs établissements. Entre forte affluence, capacités d'accueil et exigences d'un encadrement pédagogique de qualité, la situation diffère d’un établissement à un autre. La rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 a été marquée pour nombre de Collèges d’enseignement moyen (Cem) de l’académie de Dakar par une forte pression sur les capacités d'accueil. Dans les établissements visités, les responsables administratifs s'activent pour organiser la répartition des nouveaux élèves orientés en classe de 6e. Entre les inscriptions qui se poursuivent, les ajustements pédagogiques et les disponibilités en salles, les situations diffèrent d'un collège à l'autre. Au Cem Adama Ndiaye de Grand-Dakar, les 169 élèves orientés obligent déjà l'administration scolaire à envisager une nouvelle organisation des divisions. Une situation qui révèle les difficultés auxquelles certains établissements sont confrontés pour concilier l'accueil des nouveaux collégiens et la qualité des apprentissages. Dans cet établissement, le principal, Alioune Badara Mbengue, ne cache pas ses préoccupations. Habituellement, le collège fonctionne avec deux classes de 6e, mais les orientations reçues cette année risquent de modifier cette configuration. Si l'ensemble des 169 élèves confirme leur inscription, dit-il, chacune des deux divisions devrait théoriquement accueillir plus de 84 apprenants. Un effectif particulièrement élevé qui conduit l'administration à envisager l'ouverture d'une troisième classe. Cette solution permettrait de mieux répartir les nouveaux arrivants. Pour le principal, la priorité consiste d'abord à connaître le nombre réel d'élèves qui rejoindra effectivement l'établissement. Les inscriptions se poursuivent et la situation pourrait encore évoluer dans les prochains jours. Selon Alioune Badara Mbengue, certains enfants affectés au collège proviennent d'établissements privés et leurs parents préfèrent parfois les y maintenir. D'autres familles sollicitent des collèges publics d'excellence, notamment Seydou Nourou Tall. « Ces mouvements rendent difficile l'établissement d'effectifs définitifs dès les premiers jours de la rentrée », a-t-il précisé. En attendant, l'administration scolaire est en train d’examiner les possibilités d'aménagement pour éviter une concentration excessive des élèves dans les salles. Des capacités d'accueil variables selon les collèges Au Cem Blaise Diagne, la situation semble davantage maîtrisée. Le principal, Ousmane Diop, a prévu quatre classes de 6e, avec environ 50 élèves par division. L'établissement devrait ainsi accueillir près de 200 nouveaux collégiens. Un effectif important, mais que l'administration estime compatible avec ses capacités d'accueil. Selon Ousmane Diop, le collège dispose suffisamment de salles pour absorber les orientations reçues. Contrairement à certains établissements confrontés à une saturation de leurs infrastructures, Blaise Diagne possède une marge de manœuvre matérielle qui lui permet d'envisager sereinement la répartition des nouveaux élèves. « Nous ne sommes pas débordés », assure le principal, rappelant que l'établissement avait déjà fonctionné avec quatre classes de 6e lors de la précédente année scolaire. « Même en cas d'augmentation des inscriptions, la disponibilité des locaux devrait permettre de procéder aux ajustements nécessaires », note M. Diop. Toutefois, la disponibilité de salles ne règle pas entièrement la question de l'encadrement pédagogique. Avec une cinquantaine d'élèves par division, les enseignants doivent organiser leurs activités dans des groupes relativement importants. Les possibilités de pouvoir interroger individuelle les apprenants, la correction des exercices ainsi que l'accompagnement peuvent s'en trouver réduits, a indiqué M. Dione, professeur d'Histoire et géographie. Au Cem Mathurin Diop de Dakar, la principale, Mme Bâ, affiche également une certaine sérénité. L'établissement dispose de quatre classes de 6e et ne signale pas de difficulté majeure pour accueillir les nouveaux arrivants. Les dispositions pédagogiques sont prises et les salles disponibles permettent d'envisager une répartition des élèves sans pression. Le défi pédagogique du suivi individualisé Au-delà des chiffres, la question des effectifs pléthoriques renvoie directement aux conditions d'apprentissage. La classe de sixième constitue une étape déterminante dans le parcours scolaire. Les élèves quittent l'environnement de l'école élémentaire pour découvrir un fonctionnement différent, marqué par la multiplication des enseignants, la diversification des disciplines et de nouvelles exigences en matière d'autonomie. Dans des classes de 50 à 60 élèves, cette transition peut devenir plus difficile à accompagner. Les enseignants doivent composer avec des niveaux d'acquisition hétérogènes, des rythmes d'apprentissage différents et des besoins d'encadrement parfois importants, a fait savoir le principal de Blaise Diagne. Le temps disponible pour chaque apprenant se réduit également au fur et à mesure que les effectifs augmentent. La pression sur les effectifs prend une dimension particulièrement visible au Cem John Fitzgerald Kennedy. Dans cet établissement très sollicité de Dakar, les trois classes de 6e comptent déjà 60 élèves chacune. Au total, 180 nouveaux collégiens y sont répartis dans trois divisions, alors que les demandes d'inscription continuent d'affluer. La principale, Aminata Sar Kanté, reconnaît que cette forte affluence constitue un des défis majeurs en ce début d’année scolaire. L'établissement, a-t-elle fait savoir, attire chaque année de nombreuses familles dont certaines sollicitent une place plusieurs mois avant l'ouverture des classes. Les orientations reçues viennent ainsi s'ajouter aux demandes d'admission formulées directement par les parents. Cette attractivité s'explique notamment par l'offre pédagogique développée dans cet établissement. Depuis plusieurs années, note la principale, Kennedy propose des activités de robotique, d'informatique, d'intelligence artificielle, d'entrepreneuriat et de développement personnel. « Des initiatives qui suscitent l'intérêt des familles », dit-elle, soulignant que cette situation pose des exigences particulières en matière d'encadrement. « Avec 60 élèves dans une même salle, le suivi individualisé devient plus complexe. Les enseignants doivent assurer la progression des programmes tout en veillant à l'adaptation des nouveaux collégiens, dont les niveaux et les besoins peuvent varier considérablement », a indiqué Mme Kanté. Consciente de ces difficultés, Aminata Sarr Kanté entend renforcer les dispositifs d'accompagnement. L'établissement a placé la prévention du décrochage scolaire au cœur de ses priorités pour cette année. Sous le thème « Repérer, accompagner et agir », des séances bimensuelles doivent associer conseillers d'orientation, psychologues et parents autour des élèves identifiés comme étant en difficulté. Cette initiative, affirme la responsable de l’établissement, vise à prévenir les risques d'abandon et à assurer un suivi des apprenants confrontés à des contraintes scolaires, sociales ou familiales. Dans un contexte de classes fortement chargées, elle apparaît comme une réponse à la nécessité de maintenir une attention particulière aux parcours individuels. Pour la principale, l'enjeu reste de garantir les mêmes chances de réussite à tous les élèves, indépendamment de leurs résultats antérieurs ou de leur origine scolaire. Une ambition qui suppose de concilier l'ouverture de l'établissement au plus grand nombre avec les exigences d'un encadrement de qualité. Daouda DIOUF

items.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. The post Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects appeared first on Vanguard News .
